name: Python
typeSystem: Dynamic, strong, duck-typed. Types are checked at runtime, but optional type hints (PEP 484) let external tools like mypy or Pyright check code statically without changing execution.

typeSystemExample.caption: Generic max: duck-typed, with optional type hints
typeSystemExample.source:
from typing import TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T", int, float, str)

def max_of(a: T, b: T) -> T:
    return a if a >= b else b

print(max_of(3, 7))
print(max_of(1.5, 2.8))

runtime: CPython compiles source to bytecode executed by its virtual machine. PyPy adds a tracing JIT, while Cython and Nuitka use C/C++ toolchains to produce native extension modules or executables.

runtimes.name: CPython
runtimes.role: Reference implementation: compiles to bytecode run by a stack-based VM.

runtimes.name: PyPy
runtimes.role: Alternative Python implementation with a tracing JIT.

runtimes.name: Cython / Nuitka
runtimes.role: Cython translates Python-like, optionally annotated code to C for extension modules; Nuitka translates Python programs to C and builds extension modules or executables.

runtimes.name: MicroPython
runtimes.role: Compiles to MicroPython bytecode executed by its VM by default, with optional native emitters.

compilers.name: CPython
compilers.role: Reference bytecode compiler and virtual machine.

compilers.name: PyPy
compilers.role: RPython-based implementation with a just-in-time compiler.

compilers.name: Cython
compilers.role: Compiles annotated Python to C for native extension modules.

compilers.name: Nuitka
compilers.role: Whole-program compiler translating Python to C-level code.

compilers.name: mypyc
compilers.role: Compiles type-annotated Python to fast C extensions.

asyncRuntimes.name: asyncio
asyncRuntimes.role: Standard library event loop for cooperative async I/O (the default for async/await).

asyncRuntimes.name: uvloop
asyncRuntimes.role: Drop-in asyncio replacement built on libuv; 2-4x faster than the default loop.

asyncRuntimes.name: Trio
asyncRuntimes.role: Structured concurrency library with strict task management and clear cancellation semantics.

asyncRuntimes.name: AnyIO
asyncRuntimes.role: Compatibility layer that runs the same async code on asyncio or Trio.

concurrencyModel: In standard GIL-enabled CPython builds, one thread executes Python bytecode at a time, though threads can overlap I/O; multiprocessing is commonly used for CPU parallelism. asyncio provides cooperative concurrency, usually on one event-loop thread.

concurrencyExample.caption: 4 cooperatively scheduled tasks computing i*i via asyncio
concurrencyExample.source:
import asyncio

async def square(n: int) -> int:
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return n * n

async def main():
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(square(i) for i in range(4)))
    print(*results)

asyncio.run(main())
